title: Autoscale oscillation detection and long-tail soak for Dedicated capacity
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a robust load-testing harness focused on Dedicated capacity that validates autoscaling behavior under combined burst + steady-state patterns and identifies regressions in throughput (tokens/sec) and tail latency (p95, p99). This ticket covers: (1) deterministic burst profiles that exercise quick scale-up and scale-down, (2) prolonged soak runs to reveal slow regressions or resource leaks over 24–72h, (3) oscillation detection for autoscaler flapping (rapid up/down cycles), and (4) regression detection algorithm tuned for tokens/sec and p95 shifts tied to code/model/kernel changes.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline established: canonical steady-state tokens/sec and p95 measured across three independent runs within ±5%
Regression detector flags a change when tokens/sec drops >10% sustained for 10 minutes or p95 increases >30% sustained for 5 minutes
Autoscale stabilization time (cold→steady capacity) < 90s for typical burst profile, measured median over 10 bursts
Oscillation detector fires when >3 scale up/down cycles occur within 30 minutes and creates an incident ticket automatically
Soak test runbook and dashboard published; 48h soak completed with resource leak check and post-run perf diff report
Integration: load harness posts metrics to Console ingestion endpoint and tests appear on per-model throughput dashboard
tasks: Design burst + steady-state traffic patterns (spikes, ramp, sawtooth, poisson bursts)
Implement generator that emits token-level workload while varying prompt length and KV cache warm/cold states
Instrument generator with synthetic traces to correlate request start/end with autoscaler events
Create regression detection pipeline: rolling-window baselines, EWMA control limits, and lookback comparison to last known-good run
Add oscillation detector that monitors scale events and suppresses false positives during planned maintenance
Wire results into Console: charts for tokens/sec, p95/p99, scale events, GPU utilization, and cost per token
Run three baseline runs, tune detector thresholds, and record baseline artifacts (logs, playback scripts)
Execute 48h soak and a 72h extended soak, capture heap/ephemeral disk/gpu memory trends
Write runbook for triage, automated rollback criteria, and follow-up remediation tasks
env_setup: Dedicated test cluster in staging region eu-west-1 with 6 node pool (G5x2-equivalent). Kube namespace: perf-dedicated-osc-test. Ingest keys and endpoint scoped to test org. Enable KV cache metric emission and runtime debug flags for kernel selection logging.
run_plan: Phase 1: Establish baseline with 3x 2-hour steady-state runs at target load. Phase 2: Run burst profile (10s ramp to 3x steady) repeated 10x to measure scale latency. Phase 3: 48h soak with hourly microbursts and tail-case prompts; collect continuous metrics. Phase 4: Extended 72h run if Phase 3 shows anomalies. After runs, execute regression detector and produce performance diff report.
regression_detection_strategy: Use a two-tier detector: short-term (10m EWMA) for immediate regressions and long-term (24h rolling baseline) for slow regressions. Trigger alerts for sustained violations. Maintain an artifacts store of 'last-known-good' runs; run statistical tests (Mann-Whitney U) on tokens/sec and p95 distributions and surface effect size & confidence. Attach failing request samples and top-10 slow prompts for triage.
observability_integration: Emit test-run tags to Console with test_id; ensure traces include autoscaler event ids. Create Grafana dashboard with comparison mode to overlay baseline and current run. Hook regression detector to PagerDuty test escalation with a low-severity channel for initial runs.
notes: Observed noisy p95 from kernel fallback path during previous soak (see ENG-9273 notes) — include synthetic traffic that hits fallback
Coordinate maintenance windows with infra because scale tests can trigger autoscaling policies that affect other teams
